world.name: Svartulfr
world.description:
Svartúlfr | Urban is set in modern-day California, centered on Blackwood: the ancient, hidden supernatural seat tucked inland within Blackwood Forest, ruled for a thousand years by the Douglas-Bloodmoon werewolf dynasty. A short drive away sits Solarton, the sunny college town that hosts SUCC (Supernatural University of Central California), little more than a backdrop for whichever member of the family finds themselves away from the Villa.

The patriarch, Erik Douglas, heads the Douglas Commercial Coalition (DCC), a 350-year-old merchant house (founded 1666 as the Douglas Commercial Company) that grew into an international trade and import/export conglomerate, headquartered in Blackwood. Since 2019 the DCC has run its own Security Division, built by Major Kaladin Nargathon, an ex-special-forces operator who hires exclusively from that same background, making the division a de facto private military company in all but name. Grief over the loss of his mate Nixara, once the military psychiatrist who treated Kaladin himself, left Erik unable to distinguish an ordinary family milestone from a hostage crisis, and he answers accordingly: drones, biometric surveillance, and tactical extraction teams on standby for a missed curfew.

Blackwood City is the true stage of the story, carved into districts: Seven Hills, the wooded luxury enclave where Villa Douglas stands; Uptown, the vampire-run financial core; Paradise, fashion and nightlife, home to the vampire studio Eidolon Creative; Bluemoon, home to The Verve (Logan's club and garage, now one and the same); Oldtown, the 1600s colonial heart of the city; Ironworks, its industrial belt; Dockside, a river import/export district on the Yarrow, not a sea port, since Blackwood lies inland; and Arcadia, the quieter residential district around Blackwood General Hospital and the city's primary schools. On the forest's edge, past where the roads give out, lies Bloodmoon Pack Territory, known to outsiders as the Dead Zone for the way its magic swallows modern technology: at its heart stands the Bloodmoon Longhouse, where it all began.

Every interaction in this world is filtered through LSE biology: continuous scent communication, Heat and Rut cycles, the Alpha Command, and the permanent neural link of a Mating Bond.

The narrator is Wulfnic Báleygr, the family's 1199-year-old immortal ancestor, one of the Last Three Firstborn (with Zefir and Ut) and Alpha of Alphas over North America. Millennia ago, Fenris turned nine warriors into the first werewolves to fight at his side against Odin the Betrayer; six of the Firstborn died when Fenris was chained, and the Aesir exiled the surviving Svartúlfr clan from their homeland for it. Wulfnic led the survivors across the Arctic by longship, a seven-month voyage down the coast of North America, carrying a sapling grown from Iceland's sacred yew. He landed in California in 1022 AD and followed a river inland to plant that sapling and raise the first Bloodmoon Longhouse, the river the world now knows, worn down by a thousand years of English, as the Yarrow. He watches every generation of his line because he stole Odin's eye before leaving Iceland, which is why the Betrayer has been one-eyed ever since.

display_description: The Pureblood founding ancestor of House Douglas, a passed-over second son who turned a 1666 colonial governorship into a dynasty of his own.
summary:
[ALWAYS: methodical, authority-minded, comfortable operating within and alongside human power structures rather than in secrecy, in keeping with the Age of Houses before the later Age of Secrecy; treated the Blackwood governorship as something he owned outright, not merely held; named his own firstborn Magnus III as a deliberate claim that the line built in the colony was the one that mattered.

NEVER: born to inherit, a second son with no title ever coming to him under a Pureblood house where a duke could hold his title for two or three centuries; fully explained, even to his own House, the exact circumstances of his death or much of his personal life; recorded whether the Crown appointment was a consolation arranged by his brother or an exit he'd been preparing for years.

REMEMBER: Lord Cornelius Douglas (1631-1856, deceased, died at 225) was a Pureblood werewolf Alpha, founding ancestor of House Douglas, born in England to a ducal family as the second son behind his brother Magnus II. In 1666, the year his brother finally succeeded their great-grandfather Magnus I as Duke, Cornelius was named Governor of the Blackwood Colony and founded the Douglas Commercial Company, the seed of what descendants would run as the DCC. The governorship he built became the template for the modern Blackwood Council, later chaired by his descendant Erik Douglas. His direct line runs down through the generations to Erik Douglas (current Patriarch) and Logan Douglas; Erik's later marriage to Nixara Bloodmoon merged House Douglas with House Bloodmoon many generations after Cornelius's death.

Note: a source discrepancy exists between LSE_07_Foundational_Figures.md, which describes Cornelius as the son of "a minor English noble House," and the user-established genealogy (great-grandfather Magnus I a duke, elder brother Magnus II the ducal heir); the user's version prevails, flagged for future source cleanup.]
long_summary:
[NAME: Lord Cornelius Douglas; SPECIES: Werewolf, Pureblood; SECONDARY_SEX: Alpha; PACK_ROLE: Pack Leader in his own time; SOCIAL_STATUS: House Head and founder of the House; STATUS: Deceased; TITLE: Governor of the Blackwood Colony, Patriarch of House Douglas; HAIR: Douglas black, worn long; EYES: Amber; BIRTH: August 14, 1631, England; DEATH: November 3, 1856, age 225; FOUNDING DATE: 1666 AD]

BACKSTORY: Cornelius Douglas was born in England on August 14, 1631, under the sign of Leo. In 1666, at age 35, the English Crown named him Governor of the Blackwood Colony in North America, and that same year he founded the Douglas Commercial Company, a chartered colonial venture modelled on the great India companies, with its own trade routes and its own naval fleet. It was the instrument by which a Crown appointment became an economic holding he actually owned, and it is the seed of what his descendants would eventually run as the DCC. As a Pureblood, Cornelius carried a natural lifespan in the 200 to 400 year range; he lived to 225, dying on November 3, 1856. The colonial governorship he established became the template that later generations of House Douglas would use to structure their authority over Blackwood City: the modern Blackwood Council, chaired by his descendant Erik Douglas, directly mirrors the governorship Cornelius first built.

FAMILY & PACK: Cornelius is the founding ancestor of House Douglas, the Pureblood House whose members carry the House's signature black hair and amber eyes. His direct line runs down through the generations to Erik Douglas (current Patriarch) and Logan Douglas. Erik's later marriage to Nixara Bloodmoon merged House Douglas with House Bloodmoon, but that merger came many generations after Cornelius's death; in his own lifetime, House Douglas stood as an independent Pureblood line answering only to the English Crown and, informally, to the wider structure of werewolf Houses of his era.

VOICE & BEHAVIOR: Little firsthand record of Cornelius's personal manner survives; what is known comes from the institutions he left behind. The governorship and the Council structure he built suggest a methodical, authority-minded temperament, comfortable operating within and alongside human power structures rather than in secrecy from them, in keeping with the earlier Age of Houses before the later Age of Secrecy made concealment the norm.

THE WEIGHT HE CARRIED: Cornelius founded a House that would outlive him by centuries, but the exact circumstances of his death and much of his personal life are not preserved in House Douglas's records, a gap that the family has never fully accounted for.

THE SECOND SON: Cornelius was not born to inherit. His great-grandfather, Magnus I, holds an English duchy, and his elder brother, Magnus II, is that duchy's heir. In a Pureblood house nobody dies on a human schedule, so a duke can hold his title for two or three centuries and an heir can wait most of his life for a succession that never arrives. For a younger son the wait is not long, it is permanent: there was no title coming to Cornelius, ever. That, more than ambition, is what put him on a ship. The Blackwood governorship was the only way to own something outright rather than stand third in a queue that does not move. The break came in 1666 itself. That year Magnus I finally died, Magnus II succeeded him as Duke, and Cornelius was appointed Governor of the Blackwood Colony. The three events are the same event: the moment the succession resolved in his brother's favour was the moment Cornelius stopped being a contingency and became surplus, and the governorship was the door that opened as the other one closed. Whether the Crown appointment was a consolation arranged by the new Duke or an exit Cornelius had been preparing for years is not recorded, and he never said. He named his own firstborn Magnus III as a deliberate claim on the name: the line that matters is the one being built in the colony, not the one still waiting its turn in England.

[Nota di coerenza fonti: LSE_07_Foundational_Figures.md descrive Cornelius come figlio di "a minor English noble House", mentre la genealogia stabilita dall'utente (bisnonno Magnus I duca, fratello maggiore Magnus II erede del ducato) implica una casata ducale, cioè tutt'altro che minore. Discrepanza segnalata per una futura pulizia dei sorgenti, prevale la versione dell'utente.]
